# dsh-session-management
> English | 简体中文
A session-management plugin for the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).
List, archive, pin, stop, rename, and **permanently delete** your `dsh` sessions — from a **Settings
page**, the **sidebar right-click menu**, the **`/sessions` command**, or the **`session_manage` to
ol** the AI can call for you.
`dsh` only ships *Archive* for sessions. This plugin adds the missing part: a real delete (removes t
he session log from disk), plus a bird's-eye view of every session with its size, status, and log pa
session log from disk), plus a bird's-eye view of every session with its size, status, and log path.
## Features
| Action | What it does |
| **list** | Every session with title, id, cwd, live/cold, running, pinned, archived, event count, o

n-disk size, and log path. Text search, optional "show archived". |
| **archive / unarchive** | Reve

rsible — hides a session from the sidebar without touching its history. |
| **pin / unpin** | Keep s

essions at the top of the sidebar. |
| **stop** | Interrupt a running session's current turn (same a

s the user's stop button). |
| **rename** | Update a live session title (written to the session log,

durable). |
| **delete** | Permanently remove the session log directory from disk. **Irreversible**
— every entry point requires an explicit confirmation. A running session is stopped first. Deleting
the *current* session is allowed; its in-memory copy disappears on the next app restart. |
All four entry points share one operation core in the Host, so the page, the menu, the command, and
the AI tool always behave identically. The UI follows the Harness language setting (English / 中文 swi
tch live, no reload).

## Requirements

- A `dsh` profile with the Web GUI (the standard `dsh web` composition or Desktop).
- The shipped JS
ONL session-persistence backend (the default) — needed to see cold sessions, disk sizes, and to dele

te stored logs. Without it, everything except `delete` still works on live sessions.
- Built against
`@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.2`. The plugin registers only through stable Host services (tools, commands,
slots, context menus, web routes) and imports **no internal packages** at runtime.

Or install from a checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **From an interactive `dsh` session (recommended)** — tell the AI:
> install the plugin bundle at

/abs/path/to/dsh-session-management
- **From the Web GUI** — open **Settings → Plugins** and install
this directory like any bundle.
**Restart `dsh` and refresh the browser page.** A bundle with both a Host and a Client half needs a
restart on first install so the module graph picks the halves up.
After the restart you get all four surfaces at once:

- **Settings → "Session management"** — the management page
- **Sidebar right-click** — a red **Dele

te session** item above the built-in Archive
- **`/sessions`** — the slash command
- **`session_mana
ge`** — the agent tool
> **Note** — if you previously installed a copy of this plugin under another name (e.g. `@local/dsh-
session-management`), remove that bundle first. Two active copies both registering `session_manage`
collide at activation.
## Usage
### Settings page
**Settings → Session management**: a searchable table of every session. Each row carries Archive / U
narchive / Pin / Unpin / Stop / Rename / Delete buttons; Delete needs an in-row "Confirm delete". Th
e page language follows your browser (English / 中文).
### Sidebar menu
Right-click any session row in the sidebar — the menu gains a red **Delete session** row above the b
session row in the sidebar — the menu gains a red **Delete session** row above the built-in Archive:

> … **Delete session** ← added by this plugin
> Archive session  `Ctrl + Shift + A`
Selecting it raises a confirmation toast — press **Confirm delete** to remove the log permanently.
### Slash command
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`delete` refuses to run without the trailing `confirm`. An empty id for `archive` / `pin` / `stop` a
cts on the current session.
## How it works
The plugin composes with existing `dsh` services instead of reaching around them:
| Concern | Service used |
| Session enumeration + titles | `sessionQuery.listSessions()` (live-preferred), `readTitleSnapshots

()` |
| Archive / pin state | `workspaceRegistry.archiveSession/unarchiveSession/pinSession/unpinSes

sion`, `archivedSessionIds`, `pinnedSessionIds` |
| Stop | `ctx.agents.get(id)` → `agent.cancel({ ki

nd: 'user' })` |
| Rename | `sessionTitle.rename(session, title)` — a durable title event |
| Delete
| `sessionPersistence.list()` → each stored session's `location.path` (e.g. `~/.dsh/sessions/--<cwd
>--/<id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`); the plugin removes that whole session-owned directory after checki
ng the artifact name shape. The persistence seam has no delete API, so this is an intentionally guar

ded direct removal. |
| Page transport | a JSON API served at `/dsh-session-management/api` on the H

arness webserver, guarded by a same-origin (`Origin`/`Host`) check |
| Sidebar menu | `contextMenus.
register({ target: 'session' })` with a two-step confirm via the host toast |
Session ids are opaque — some are plain UUIDs without the `session-` prefix. The plugin always uses
the exact id the list reported and never rewrites it.
